name: Stand-up paddleboard
blurb: The easiest way onto the water. Standing up takes one session; paddling in a straight line without switching sides every three strokes takes a few more.
gear: A leash — it keeps you attached to your flotation
A buoyancy aid and appropriate clothing
steps: Start kneeling in flat, sheltered water and paddle until the board feels stable.
Stand by moving one foot at a time to where your knees were, feet hip-width, parallel, mid-board.
Look at the horizon, not your feet. Knees soft, hips loose, weight centred.
Learn the paddle grip: one hand on the top, one on the shaft, and the blade angled away from you, not towards you.
Paddle with torso rotation, planting the blade well forward and pulling to your feet.
Learn to turn with a sweep stroke and a step back, and always wear the leash.
tips: Almost everyone holds the paddle backwards at first. The blade angles forward, away from the handle.
Offshore wind is the danger on a paddleboard — it is easy to get blown out and impossible to paddle back. Check the forecast.
proof: You paddle a kilometre standing, turning at each end, without falling in.
